summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder managed with a chronic Foley catheter, was admitted for weakness and fatigue, which he recognized as typical symptoms of a urinary tract infection. He reported transient hematuria and had not been taking his methenamine due to a lapse in prescription. Initial labs showed marked leukocytosis and pyuria, prompting IV antibiotics and fluid resuscitation. A chest X-ray ruled out pneumonia. His Foley catheter was replaced, and he was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics. Urine culture grew Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Enterococcus species. Antibiotics were de-escalated to oral ciprofloxacin and amoxicillin-clavulanate based on sensitivities, with addition of methenamine for prophylaxis. His symptoms resolved, and he returned to baseline. He was discharged home with home services, continuing all baseline medications and a plan for follow-up with his primary care provider.
